newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 14.90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 14.90 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 14.90 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 11.15 percent on Friday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 17.50 percent against 15.9 percent on Friday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said the market remained short of ringgit funds following the central Bank Negara's buying of the currency last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers were estimating between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit went out of the system.
Dealers said there was confusion over where rates are heading after Bank Negara did not intervene in the fall of the ringgit against the dollar on Monday's trading.
The ringgit plunged to a 16-month low at 2.55 a dollar, from 2.5042/52 at the end of Kuala Lumpur trading on Friday, when the central bank did not prevent heavy selling of the ringgit.
Around 0350 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5370/00 a dollar.
"They have said that reserves are enough to defend the ringgit and speculators will lose. Now there's confusion on what they want," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Some dealers said the central bank was probably being realistic when it did not try to defend a particular level for the ringgit.
"You can have all the amount of reserves, but you cannot fight the world," said another dealer.
The dealers said activities in the money market were mainly centred on the one-week and one-month rates. "Nobody dares to take beyond one-month because it is too expensive," one dealer said.
The one-month rate was dealing at 15/17 percent around 0330 GMT, after falling on lending by a large agent bank of Bank Negara. It traded at 15/20 percent on Friday.
"I think they (Bank Negara) are in the market to guide rates lower," said a dealer. "They are lending at the one-month."
One-week money was at 20/25 percent and three-month indicated at 10/13 percent.
One-month swap was steady at 200/280.
Dealers said there were rumours that the central bank was meeting with senior Malaysian bankers to discuss market volatility on Monday.
But a banking source said no such meeting was taking place and none was scheduled.
"There's no meeting, so far there's nothing. There's no scheduled meeting (on Monday)," he said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange dropped to reflect future expectations of firmer rates.
The three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down 15 basis points to 92.15, or an implied yield of 7.85 percent.
The December contract fell 12 to 92.43, or 7.57 percent.
